newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Migros gets Globus majority, makes offer.
newsitem.headline: Migros gets Globus majority, makes offer.

text.p: Swiss retailing cooperative Migros-Genossenschafts-Bund said it had made an agreed offer to buy 53.8 percent of the voting capital of fellow retailer Magazine zum Globus.
It was offering to buy all other outstanding shares at 1,180 Swiss francs per registered share and 1,080 francs per participation certificate, it said in a statement.

"Migros made an offer to Magazine zum Globus's pool shareholders and board to buy 53.8 percent of the voting capital or 28.6 percent of the capital. Pool shareholders accepted the offer," the companies said in a joint statement.
Migros gave assurances it would make an offer for other outstanding shares in line with the Swiss takeover code.
"Globus's board recommends holders of shares and participation certificates accept the offer," it added.
It said the offer represented a premium of 25 percent over current market prices. Registered shares closed yesterday at 900, while non-voting certificates closed at 820.
The price "is considered fair based on Globus's internal calculations and reflects prospects for development in the context of restructuring processes now under way in the Globus group," it said.
Globus plunged to a group net loss of 179.4 million francs in the year ended in February 1997. This included reserves and extraordinary costs totaling 166.3 million.
